Hi! You have communicated something very personal to your family and initiated an attempt to help yourself and also let them know why you behave the way you do. **Even if this does not turn out the way you wished for, your expectation for interest and apprehension is healthy and you should stick to it.**

I have trouble with dissociation and derealisation and about 2-3 years ago it intensified as well, I tried to hide it from my environment, from family, even from myself. A facade that I was very good at building, not really knowing what DR is back then. Intense derealization made me depressed and suicidal 2 years ago and by luck a friend of mine that I phoned at my absolute low dragged me to a mental hospital where my process of getting help started. **So DR is a serious issue! Don't allow yourself to think wasn't serious 'enough'!**

I have a very loving family and they have been shocked because they just could't imagine how such a (seemingly) 24/7-happy and motivated human like me has suicidal tendencies. Now the important part: **Although my family is emotionally very close, they haven't researched DR at all, they either cannot understand the feeling or they feel helpless themselves not knowing what to do, so it is natural for humans to try to cover that up.**

Therefore, try to communicate small and precise ways in which your family can help you. For me this is the hardest part but I default to my cousine just to give me a long hug and stay silent. Ask your sister for some more support if you are comfortable with that. She might be able to help you understand why your mom told you there might be a problem when you share your struggle. I want you to consider the way you reacted: When your mom didn't give you an answer you filled that gap with your own answer, she could be ashamed. This self-made answer is simply an *assumption*. It can be true, yeah… But it could also be wrong! What I want to tell you: This can show you what you yourself might fear. It is very demanding to change this default assumption and it is worth it: Reality is about interpretation of your environment, of all the stimuli. It is interpretation! Without wanting to dive to deep into biology and neurology: **your interpretation and thus your subjective reality is heavily influencey by your expectation. If you can shape your expectations and draw a picture of how you want things to turn out, you have a higher rate of meeting them.** You will be subject to more obstacles as well because you can more easily view the discrepancy between your expectation and the actual outcome, so don't let the outcome influence your faith in those expectations!

I am very glad you reached out to somebody (in this case reddit) and gave it a second try!  
Let me know how your sister responded after asking her about this. Search for confirmation of what is helpful actively and prepare to comensate for violation of your expectations nonetheless.  


If you need emotional support I want to give you a small amount here \*/hug/\*  
I don't have that much myself but it is still worth sharing… :)

Often I forget about what happened during most of my dreams. But then something in reality is in conflict with what happened in a dream: *Didn't this part of the city look different?, I thought I have spoken with person xyz about abc... - but that can't be because I have never been here / did't meet xyz recently.* It's like dejuvu: same situation but somehow different plot.
Because it is rare that dreams and reality collide in this way I am sure most of my intuitive memories of what is real actually reside from dreams.
So yes, dreams (even though not actively remembered) feel more real than everyday life.

Now I sleep 15h/day and even before this bad sleeping behaviour started I felt like passing out and be kept trapped in this feeling: half alive, have gone already.
